claims.text: The initial alloy has the nominal composition (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The unmodified alloy has high caloric performance under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
The unmodified alloy has poor mechanical integrity and is prone to cracking under load.
Adding a small amount of Cu will produce a dispersed, ductile copper phase in the alloy.
The dispersed copper phase will enhance toughness and mitigate crack propagation.
The copper phase will absorb and redistribute mechanical stress.
Stress absorption and redistribution by the copper phase will blunt crack initiation and growth.
The copper phase will minimally interfere with the phase-transformation mechanisms responsible for the caloric response.
Cu addition will increase compressive strength by roughly 20% or more relative to the unmodified alloy.
The caloric response of the Cu-modified alloy will remain within about 10% of that of the unmodified alloy.
The intervention is expected to remain effective during applied-field and pressure-field operation, under compressive loading, from room temperature to approximately 300°C.
The intervention's effects may change under extreme fields, temperatures, or loads.
